transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Liu (Redwood CSM); Elena Torres (SilverLake Head of Eng), Daniel Kim (Security Lead), Priya Shah (PM), Marcus Lee (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate your time. quick sanity check on audio?
[00:05] Elena: yep can hear you, thanks Maya.
[00:12] Maya: cool. objective for today is to finalize security scope for the pilot and confirm workload sizing + benchmarks so we can get an accurate timeline. Ravi will cover the benchmark plan.
[00:25] Ravi: great, i'll be brief then dive into numbers. one note up front: we support hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem). for regulated workloads like healthcare we usually recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private depending on customer KMS/HSM needs and network isolation.
[00:40] Daniel: right — key must-haves for us are SOC 2 or ISO attestation, SSO/SAML with SCIM for provisioning, fine-grained RBAC, full audit logs with immutable retention options, and KMS integration. also data residency — pilot needs to run in us-east or on-prem.
[01:05] Maya: makes sense. we'll share our SOC2 report and ISO27001 cert; those are standard. for SAML SSO we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for groups; RBAC can be scoped by role. audit logs include per-request metadata, user id, timestamps, and can be exported to your SIEM. retention SLA is configurable for Dedicated/Private.
[01:32] Priya: on audit logs — we need the ability to capture request/response hashes and user mapping, but not store PII from patient data. is there a recommended approach?
[01:40] Ravi: yes, two patterns. 1) piping logs to your SIEM and having Redwood redact at ingestion, or 2) using our built-in prefix/KV cache + request masking where you supply a PII mask function client-side. we don't recommend storing raw PHI in logs.
[02:05] Marcus: can you do server-side KMS where keys never leave our control?
[02:10] Maya: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Dedicated and Private — keys can be in AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or an HSM for on-prem. with Private we can do full key isolation.
[02:30] Elena: timeline question — if we sign pilot, how fast can you spin up Dedicated capacity in our region?
[02:36] Ravi: typical lead time is 2-3 weeks for dedicated reservation in a new region, faster if we're using existing capacity. for Private on-prem it's longer (4-8 weeks) because of networking and OIDC integration. for the pilot we usually do a 3-6 week scoped pilot.
[02:55] Daniel: for compliance we'll need contract language around data handling and breach notifications. do you have a template?
[03:02] Maya: yes we'll share the security pack and data processing addendum; legal can follow up.
[03:10] Priya: success criteria — we need clear pass/fail metrics. our product team wants latency p95 <200ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and throughput to handle burst of roughly 150 requests/min with average 800 tokens per request. accuracy/regression — must not degrade model quality compared to our current baseline. cost is also a factor.
[03:35] Ravi: ok on workloads. for sizing, for 150 req/min average 800 tokens, that's ~120k tokens/min peak which is about 7.2M tokens/hr. For benchmarking we recommend running: a) short prompt latency tests (<=128 tokens) for p50/p95/p99, b) mixed workload sim with 800-token average to measure throughput and cost, and c) long context tests up to 4k tokens to validate KV cache behavior.
[04:10] Marcus: do you have examples of cost per 1k tokens on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:15] Ravi: rough numbers: on hosted you'd see higher unit costs but less setup; Dedicated typically reduces per-token cost by 30-50% depending on utilization and quantization. we'll provide a cost-latency spreadsheet from last pilot to give ballpark.
[04:35] Elena: we'd like to run the benchmark on a comparable infra — 4xA100 and a 2xT4 config, please.
[04:40] Ravi: that's fine. we'll run both and include wall-clock latency, GPU utilization, memory/kv-hit rates, and per-1k-token cost. note: KV cache hits will dramatically reduce cost for conversational flows.
[05:00] Priya: for privacy we're considering client-side PII masking before sending to Redwood, and maybe token-level redaction. any limits?
[05:08] Ravi: client-side masking is recommended. on our side we can also enforce request filters and block certain pattern matches. the transcription sometimes shows product names — small heads up, our internal transcripts sometimes say "Redwood Dedicate" or "kay-vee cache" in auto-ml text, just ignore that.
[05:28] Maya: ha yes auto-transcribe flubs.
[05:30] Daniel: audit logs — what fields do you capture?
[05:33] Ravi: we capture timestamp, request id, route/model id, token counts, request metadata (user id if provided), latency, GPU node id obfuscated, and an event trail for model rollout decisions. we can add request/response hash and a pointer to log storage. for immutable retention we can export to S3 with write-once policies.
[06:00] Elena: SOC 2 — does Redwood have the latest report and do you do scoped SOC for Dedicated customers?
[06:07] Maya: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certs; we'll send redacted reports. Dedicated customers can get additional controls documented in the contract.
[06:16] Priya: will you require an NDA before we share sample prompts with PHI?
[06:20] Jordan: good question — yes let's do an NDA; we can also accept a DPA. we typically sign a mutual NDA prior to receiving PHI-like payloads.
[06:35] Daniel: about SSO — we use Okta. how long to integrate SAML + SCIM?
[06:40] Ravi: SAML is quick (1-2 business days to configure SSO once SAML metadata is provided). SCIM provisioning can take a week depending on group mappings. for RBAC we map Okta groups to Redwood roles; we can do custom roles for your needs.
[07:00] Elena: success criteria recap — security ok (SOC2/ISO attestation + DPA), SSO + SCIM working, audit log export to our SIEM with required fields, benchmarks that meet latency/throughput targets, and cost within agreed threshold.
[07:15] Maya: that's a good summary. for benchmarks we'll need 3 things from you: sample prompt set, target success metrics (latency/cost/quality thresholds), and any blocked PII patterns.
[07:30] Priya: i'll gather those and send by Tue.
[07:34] Maya: perfect. i'll summarize next steps in email.

[10:12] (Ravi walks through benchmark plan - mixed workload, synthetic replay of conversational flows, measures: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, kv-cache hit ratio. occasional cross talk)

[18:50] (Discussion of Private deployment tradeoffs: Private gives max isolation and key control but adds 4-8 week setup and higher cost; Dedicated hits a good balance for pilot)

[23:20] Daniel: on audit log retention we need 7 years for certain records — is that feasible?
[23:27] Maya: technically yes if you export to your own S3 and set lifecycle policies; for storage we can help with export automation.

[29:05] Elena: about legal — we need breach notification SLA 72 hours and an obligation to notify if any exfiltration may have occurred.
[29:12] Maya: standard security incident response will cover that; we'll include language in DPA.

[34:00] (Bench metrics discussion — Ravi mentions KV cache and batching can lower cost by up to 40% in conversational workload; notes on quantization options and potential small accuracy tradeoffs)

[39:30] Priya: do you do model version pinning and rollbacks during pilot? we need stable model behavior for A/B tests.
[39:36] Ravi: yes, rollout policies, canary deploys, and automatic fallbacks. we keep model versions immutable and provide traceability per request.

[44:00] Maya: ok wrapping up — action items and owners as we'll put in the follow-up. anything else?
[44:08] Daniel: just to confirm, share SOC2/ISO + security pack and the benchmark plan.
[44:15] Maya: will do. thanks everyone.
[44:20] Elena: thanks all.

Recap / next steps: Redwood to send security docs (SOC2, ISO27001, DPA template), SE to run benchmarks on requested infra and share spreadsheet, customer to send sample prompts and PII mapping, schedule follow-up week of 2026-04-20.
notes: Transcript contains occasional auto-transcription errors (product names and acronyms). Shared artifacts: security_pack.pdf (link to be sent), benchmark_template.xlsx (to be populated by SE).
